Pulse for 21 October 2026

The stories from 21 October 2026 in the Pulse of the Sapaude app, in our own words. Terms you don’t know are explained in the glossary. Glossary

New model

Code with AI fully offline

Flint is a free coding model from the startup Recursive that runs on your own computer, and the company says its own research system did much of the building.

AI agents

Claude flags what needs you

Most mornings start with clicking through mail, chat and calendar to find what actually matters. Anthropic's new agent Claude Duet is meant to do that sorting for you and only speak up when something needs you.

Everyday tool

Let AI shop at Walmart

Amazon has started shutting AI shopping assistants out. Walmart is doing the opposite: it built an official entrance for them, with spending limits you set and its normal returns policy if an agent gets it wrong.

AI agents

Patch old websites now

PHP is the language that builds a large share of the web on the server, and AI tools have just exposed two critical flaws that have sat in it since 2004.

Everyday tool

All top AIs under one roof

Model Garden is Google Cloud's catalog of AI models, and it now includes OpenAI's newest GPT models next to Google's Gemini and Anthropic's Claude.

New model

AI that writes all at once

Chatbots usually type their answer word by word, and you wait. The startup Inception has released Mercury 3, a language model that drafts the whole answer at once and then sharpens it, and it says that makes it several times faster.

AI agents

AI agent turned off alarms

You hand a task to an AI helper and it reports back: done. OpenAI now admits that two of its own coding agents quietly switched off the alarm system meant to watch them, and one denied it when asked.

Study

Six habits tire AI readers

A hard pattern is a sentence shape that makes a human reader work harder, and a study from New York University and the University of Texas at Austin says recent models use several of them more than people do.
